arxiv-1710-03989.title: Locally Lipschitz vector optimization problems: second-order constraint qualifications, regularity condition and KKT necessary optimality conditions
arxiv-1710-03989.creator: Yi-Bin Xiao, Nguyen Van Tuyen, Jen-Chih Yao, Ching-Feng Wen
arxiv-1710-03989.description: Abstract In the present paper, we are concerned with a class of constrained vector optimization problems, where the objective functions and active constraint functions are locally Lipschitz at the referee point. Some second-order constraint qualifications of Zangwill type, Abadie type and Mangasarian – Fromovitz type as well as a regularity condition of Abadie type are proposed in a nonsmooth setting.

arxiv-2512-05227.title: Exchangeable Gaussian Processes with application to epidemics
arxiv-2512-05227.creator: Lampros Bouranis, Petros Barmpounakis, Nikolaos Demiris, Konstantinos Kalogeropoulos
arxiv-2512-05227.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lampros Bouranis, Petros Barmpounakis, Nikolaos Demiris, Konstantinos Kalogeropoulos. We develop a Bayesian non-parametric framework based on multi-task Gaussian processes, appropriate for temporal shrinkage. We focus on a particular class of dynamic hierarchical models to obtain evidence-based knowledge of infectious disease burden. These models induce a parsimonious way to capture cross-dependence between groups while retaining a natural interpretation based on an underlying mean process, itself expressed as a Gaussian process.

arxiv-2601-12426.title: Graph Attention Networks with Physical Constraints for Anomaly Detection Journal: ICT Express
arxiv-2601-12426.creator: Mohammadhossein Homaei, Iman Khazrak, Ruben Molano, Andres Caro, Mar Avila
arxiv-2601-12426.description: Abstract Water distribution systems (WDSs) face increasing cyber-physical risks, which make reliable anomaly detection essential. Many data-driven models ignore network topology and are hard to interpret, while model-based ones depend strongly on parameter accuracy. This work proposes a hydraulic-aware graph attention network using normalized conservation law violations as features.

pmc-12617989.creator: Jean Digitale, Deborah Franzon, Mark J Pletcher, Charles E McCulloch, Efstathios D Gennatas, Arriel Benis
pmc-12617989.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMissing data are a common challenge in electronic health record (EHR)–based prediction modeling. Traditional imputation methods may not suit prediction or machine learning models, and real-world use requires workflows that are implementable for both model development and real-time prediction.ObjectiveWe evaluated methods for handling missing data when using EHR data to build clinical prediction models for patients admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU).MethodsUsing EHR data containing missing values from an academic medical center PICU, we generated a synthetic complete dataset.

pmc-12960065.description: Dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON) is the most severe complication of thyroid‐associated ophthalmopathy (TAO). Although recent evidence indicates that reduced retinal capillary density (RCD) may increase DON risk independently of orbital apex crowding, the underlying mechanisms and associated metabolic reprogramming remain unclear.

pmc-12985697.title: Effect of Cutting Conditions on Roughness and Cutting Force When Machining a Freeform Surface with Barrel Tools
pmc-12985697.creator: Martin Reznicek, Cyril Horava, Jakub Zajicek, Martin Ovsik
pmc-12985697.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Barrel tools are relatively new tools that use atypical geometries to achieve shorter production times and improve surface quality. They have been increasingly used in the finishing operations industry, where they are gaining more and more popularity. For their optimal use, it is necessary to know how these tools behave during work in terms of how they load the machined product and what surface qualities they can achieve.

pmc-13256033.title: Unified characterization of the complete hierarchy of topological boundary states in a Floquet crystal
pmc-13256033.creator: Yuxiang Guo, Zhoutao Lei, Jizhou Wu, Jiankun Zhu, Yao Qin, Linhu Li, Jingyun Fan
pmc-13256033.description: Topological phases of matter are defined by bulk invariants that dictate the existence of robust boundary states. While conventional bulk–boundary correspondence links a given bulk invariant to a specific type of boundary mode, many systems may host multiple orders of topology simultaneously, including chiral edge states, weak edge states, and higher-order hinge and corner states.

pmc-13455841.title: Trace Li Pre‐Doping of Activated Carbon Cathode Enabling Accelerated Li‐Ion Transport for High‐Power Lithium‐Ion Capacitors
pmc-13455841.creator: Kyungmin Do, Jihyeon Ryu, Dong Gyun Im, Seong‐Yong Kim, Tae‐Hyun Kwon, Byeong Guk Kim, Seojin Jeon, Woosun Jang, Myoung Joon Hwang, Ki‐Hun Nam, Seung Yol Jeong, Ick‐Jun Kim, Seungwook Eom, Jaeik Hyun, Sunhye Yang
pmc-13455841.description: Rapid expansion of AI‐driven data centers demands energy storage systems that simultaneously deliver high power, safety, and practical scalability. Lithium‐ion capacitors (LICs) are attractive candidates; however, their performance is fundamentally constrained by inefficient Li pre‐doping and pore blockage in activated carbon (AC) cathodes.

pmc-13635218.title: Endogenous oxytocin-linked heart-rate synchrony and social connection during live sports spectatorship
pmc-13635218.creator: Takashi Matsui, Takafumi Yamaguchi, Daisuke Funabashi, Shion Takahashi, Hiroki Matsuoka, Ren Takamizawa, Yukina Tachibana, Shohei Dobashi, Kiyonobu Kigoshi, Shinzo Yamada, Hideki Takagi
pmc-13635218.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Oxytocin is a putative pharmacological target for social dysfunction. However, clinical trials of intranasal oxytocin have produced modest and inconsistent effects, motivating the search for naturalistic, non-pharmacological ways to recruit endogenous oxytocin. Here we show that a single session of live collegiate sports spectating is associated with endogenous oxytocin and interpersonal heart-rate (HR) synchrony, both of which were linked to psychological indices of social bonding among casual fans.

pmc-13657809.title: Kinase-based molecular subtyping and a prognostic risk model in colorectal cancer with functional validation of PLK4
pmc-13657809.creator: Chao Shen, Changmin Ding, Xiaofeng Han, Yanzhao Wang
pmc-13657809.description: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity, yet prognostic tools centered specifically on protein kinases remain scarce. This study aimed to identify kinase-related molecular subtypes of CRC and to develop and validate a kinase-based prognostic risk model integrating clinical and immune features.
